A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nonphotonic electrons at $\ensuremath{\ge}5$ Gev are not sensitive to the heavy-flavor hadron ratio.
the coalescence effect, which is important at low transverse momenta, has a negligible impact on the nonphotopic electron ${R}_{AA}$ at large transverse momentum.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the heavy flavor baryon-to-light hadron ratio does not play an important role for the electron ${R}_{{\mathit{A}}{\mathit{A}}}$.
the nonphotonic electrons are not sensitive to the heavy baryon-to-heavy meson ratios.

the heavy-flavor hadron ${R}_{\mathrm{AA}}$ and the heavy-flavour baryon-to meson ratio are not sensitive to the energy loss of heavy quarks in produced quark- gluon plasma, and thus they can be used to test the coalescence mechanism in heavy-ion collisions.
